comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: Mahé looks like a dream vacation spot, but there's so much more to life here than beautiful beaches and luxury resorts! 🌴🇸🇨 What surprised you most about everyday life in Seychelles? Could you imagine living on this island? I'd love to hear your thoughts! Thanks for watching and being part of our journey! ❤

comments.author: @WherePeopleLive8386
comments.text: The contrast at the heart of Mahé is striking: Africa's richest country on paper, yet almost everything in the shops has to be shipped in, so daily life stays expensive even with good salaries. Victoria being one of the smallest capitals in the world while the island still feels so spread out and green says a lot about how life actually works there.

comments.author: @World_Untold_321
comments.text: Those granite boulders, turquoise waters, and lush green mountains are simply incredible. I especially love seeing how Creole culture gives the Seychelles its own identity. It's not just a beautiful island destination; it's a place with a fascinating story and way of life.

comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: Imagine working all day at a beautiful beach resort while everyone around you is on vacation 😂 Anyone from Seychelles know what hotel life is actually like for the locals?

replies.author: @kelvinSeychellesIslandBoi
replies.text: @lifeonearth68 There are slow days, and then during peak season it can get hectic, I also worked a bit as a guide and skipper, getting tourists around the islands, fishing, barbequing etc. nowadays I'm a teacher, but I do still have my boat and take the kids in my basketball team and in the neighborhood for fishing every weekend, fish is found in abundance here. It's pretty nice here, until it's voting season!

replies.author: @lifeonearth68
replies.text: @kelvinSeychellesIslandBoi That's really cool, bro! 😊 People rarely get to see what goes on behind the scenes at those beautiful resorts. Was working in the kitchen pretty hectic?

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: That's exactly the kind of firsthand perspective I was hoping someone from Seychelles would share. 🇸🇨🙏 Working as a cook at Northolme Resort must have shown you a very different side of "paradise" from what guests usually see. Being in the kitchen all day probably means you experience the tourism industry more through the work behind the scenes than through the vacation atmosphere itself. Thanks for jumping in and sharing what it was actually like for you!

replies.author: @kelvinSeychellesIslandBoi
replies.text: It's pretty cool, I was a cook at the Northolme resort, I didn't get to interact with tourists that much being inside the kitchen all the time

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: For locals, working in the tourism industry means balancing those beautiful settings with the reality of long shifts, logistics, and supporting the broader island economy that keeps the country running. 🇸🇨

comments.author: @UnseenOutlands
comments.text: I never really pictured traffic and early morning commutes as part of life in Seychelles. For people traveling into Victoria every day, are public buses reliable enough to get to work and school on time? And with the island's mountainous roads, does commuting become especially difficult during heavy rain?

replies.author: @UnseenOutlands
replies.text: @squaredcircle2011 OMG, that means we’ll have to spend quite a lot of time traveling.

replies.author: @squaredcircle2011
replies.text: Well, let's just say if you live at one end of the island, you'd have to wake up at around 5am to get to Victoria before or by 8am
